question: After the sanitizer fix, should OpenClaw accept a bounded durable `gateway_restart_audit` table with redacted source/session/preflight metadata as the core restart-forensics record?
rationale: Automation can repair the nested-redaction defect, but maintainers need to own the privacy/security boundary and stored-field policy for this new persistent audit surface.

options.title: Accept after sanitizer fix
options.body: Fix nested sensitive-object redaction, keep the bounded schema, and treat restart audit rows as the core restart-forensics record.

options.title: Narrow stored metadata
options.body: Keep the table but remove or further summarize preflight/context fields before merge to reduce privacy exposure.

options.title: Pause durable storage
options.body: Pause or close this PR if restart attribution should stay in logs or wait for a broader audit-ledger design.

recommendation.title: Accept after sanitizer fix
recommendation.body: Fix nested sensitive-object redaction, keep the bounded schema, and treat restart audit rows as the core restart-forensics record.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related metadata-only audit issue and shared-state history make them the best available owner for the durable audit privacy boundary decision.
